facts.statement: A technician named Leandro Canesa discovered the Asfaltovenator skeleton in 2002 near Cerro Condor.
facts.quote: In 2002, technician Leandro Canesa discovered a theropod skeleton roughly a mile north of Cerro Condor.

facts.statement: Oliver Rauhut and Diego Pol formally named and described the species Asfaltovenator vialidadi in 2019.
facts.quote: In 2019, the type species Asfaltovenator vialidadi was named and described by Oliver Walter Mischa Rauhut and Diego Pol.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is a partial skeleton that includes a mostly complete skull, lower jaws, and the front portion of the postcranial skeleton.
facts.quote: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton with a skull, and includes the mostly complete skull and lower jaws and most of the postcranial skeleton in front of the hips

facts.statement: Asfaltovenator was a large theropod with a skull measuring 75 to 80 cm and a total body length estimated at 7 to 8 meters.
facts.quote: Asfaltovenator was a fairly large animal similar in size to Allosaurus, with the holotype skull being 75 - 80 cm in length and the total body length being estimated at 7 - 8 m.

facts.statement: The premaxillary teeth of Asfaltovenator have large serrations on the rear edge but only tiny serrations on the front edge.
facts.quote: Los dientes premaxilares tienen grandes estrías en el borde posterior, pero solo diminutas estrías en el borde delantero.

facts.statement: Asfaltovenator lived during the Middle Toarcian of the Lower Jurassic in the Cañadón Asfalto Formation of Chubut Province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Asfaltovenator (meaning "Cañadón Asfalto Formation hunter" after the fossil formation in which its fossils were found) is a genus of possibly allosauroid dinosaur from the Lower Jurassic (Middle Toarcian) Cañadón Asfalto Formation of Chubut Province, Argentina.

facts.statement: Fossils of Asfaltovenator were found in the Chacritas Member, which consists of lake and river deposits.
facts.quote: The holotype of Asfaltovenator comes from the Chacritas Member of the Cañadón Asfalto Formation. This member is mostly made up of two major depositional settings: lacustrine and fluvial deposits.

facts.statement: The lake environment where Asfaltovenator lived, known as the Chacritas Paleolake, was likely shallow, saline, or hypersaline.
facts.quote: The lacustrine section has been called the "Chacritas Paleolake", and seems to have been a rather saline or even hypersaline hydrologically closed pan lake, shallow in depth

facts.statement: In 2024, Andrea Cau proposed that Asfaltovenator belongs within Megalosauroidea as a sister taxon to Sciurumimus or within a larger stem group.
facts.quote: In 2024, Andrea Cau suggested a different position within Megalosauroidea, as a sister taxon of Sciurumimus and/or within a larger stem group.

facts.statement: The name Asfaltovenator translates to "Cañadón Asfalto Formation hunter," referencing the specific geological layer where its fossils were discovered.
facts.quote: Asfaltovenator (meaning "Cañadón Asfalto Formation hunter" after the fossil formation in which its fossils were found)

facts.statement: Preparing the Asfaltovenator fossil took five years because the stone matrix surrounding it was extremely hard.
facts.quote: It was then prepared by Mariano Caffa, a process that took five years due to the extreme hardness of the stone matrix.

facts.statement: A technician named Leandro Canesa discovered the skeleton of a theropod approximately one mile north of Cerro Cóndor in 2002.
facts.quote: En 2002, el técnico Leandro Canesa, aproximadamente a una milla al norte de Cerro Cóndor, descubrió un esqueleto de terópodo.

facts.statement: The species Asfaltovenator vialidadi was named and described by Oliver Walter Mischa Rauhut and Diego Pol in 2019.
facts.quote: En 2019, la especie tipo Asfaltovenator vialidadi fue nombrada y descrita por Oliver Walter Mischa Rauhut y Diego Pol.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found in a layer of the Cañadón Asfalto Formation dating from the Late Toarcian to the Bajocian.
facts.quote: Asfaltovenator sólo se conoce a partir del espécimen holotipo MPEF PV 3440, que se encontró en una capa de la Formación Cañadón Asfalto que data del Toarciense tardío al Bajociense.

facts.statement: The animal lived between 180.4 and 168.6 million years ago during the Toarcian to Bajocian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Bajocian (180.4 to 168.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: The known remains consist of a partial skeleton with a largely complete skull, lower jaws, and the front half of the skeleton before the hips, including ten neck vertebrae, thirteen back vertebrae, the first sacral vertebra, the complete shoulder girdle minus the furcula, and both forelimbs.
facts.quote: Consiste en un esqueleto parcial con cráneo. Contiene el cráneo en gran parte completo con las mandíbulas inferiores y la mitad frontal del esqueleto por delante de las caderas, incluidas diez vértebras del cuello, trece vértebras de la espalda y la primera vértebra sacra, la cintura escapular completa menos la furcula y ambas extremidades anteriores.

facts.statement: The skeleton also includes the distal portion of the pubic bones and a partial right hind limb consisting of the distal femur and proximal tibia and perone, plus a partial foot.
facts.quote: También la porción distal de los huesos púbicos así como una extremidad posterior derecha parcial que consiste en la porción distal del fémur y las porciones proximales de la tibia y el peroné, y un pie parcial.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis recovered Asfaltovenator as the most basal allosauroid and Megalosauroidea as a paraphyletic grade leading to Allosauroidea due to its mosaic of primitive and derived characters within Tetanurae.
facts.quote: Debido a su mosaico de caracteres primitivos y derivados dentro de Tetanurae, su inclusión en el análisis filogenético interrumpió las opiniones actuales de la filogenia tetanurana, con el análisis filogenético recuperando a Asfaltovenator como el alosauroide más basal y Megalosauroidea como un grado parafilético que conduce a Allosauroidea.

facts.statement: The genus Asfaltovenator belongs to the parent group Allosauroidea.
